blocks.text: That the cepphus is a bird of the Linnaean genus Procellaria (der Sturmvoegel [the storm-birds]) was shown by J. G. SCHNEIDER in the Leipzig Repository of Natural History (Leipziger Magazin zur Naturgeschichte und Oeconomie) for the year 1786, p. 501 ff. But whether the שחף of the Hebrews is the same bird I would neither affirm nor deny, since apart from the name nothing about this animal occurs in the Hebrew text, and Bochart's conjecture rests on no other foundation than the etymology of the word שחף. We have already seen quite often that, where the question concerns the names of animals, nothing is more uncertain than this way of reasoning.
And in OPPIAN, Ἰξευτικ. [Ixeutik.] book 2, ch. 10, p. 189, ed. Schneider.
